site.name: booking
site.summary: booking-clone Clone of the Booking.com hotel booking funnel (home → city list → area filters → detail → room → booking → confirmation), plus other business-line and supporting pages. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: search bar (destination / check-in & out dates / guests), recommended destinations, recent searches, Genius membership prompt, business-line entries in the footer | | `tokyo.html` | Tokyo hotel list: left filter panel (price, stars, rating, amenities, area), right-hand hotel cards (price, rating, review count, distance, free-cancellation tag), sort bar, map entry | | `shinjuku.html` | Shinjuku-area hotel list, same structure as above, pre-filtered to Shinjuku |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full booking system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The booking system has a mostly functional primary flow (search → hotel → room → booking → confirmation) with smooth transitions and form input handling. However, critical issues include a non-responsive 'Cancel booking' button, small mobile tap targets, and a broken sign-in flow. Recovery paths like chat/call support work, but cancellation and sign-in need fixes. Mobile layout warnings (horizontal overflow, small taps) impact usability.

exploration_plan.goal: Explore and critique the UX of the full booking system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow (home → city list → area filters → detail → room → booking → confirmation) plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed in phases: starting with the home page to validate the search flow, then moving to city/area lists to test filtering, followed by hotel detail and room selection, then booking and confirmation. Adjacent flows (flights, car rentals, attractions) will be sampled, and mobile viewport checks will repeat critical interactions.
assumptions: The primary booking flow (home → tokyo.html → shinjuku.html → hotel-detail.html → room-selection.html → reservation.html → confirmation.html) is fully navigable and representative of the system's UX.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets (e.g., top navigation links) may cause usability issues on mobile. Forms (e.g., reservation details) may have validation or accessibility gaps.

phases.title: Home Page & Search Flow
phases.objective: Validate the home page's search functionality, navigation, and responsive layout (desktop/mobile).
key_checks: Interact with the search bar (destination, dates, guests) and click 'Search' to ensure it navigates to tokyo.html. Test top navigation links (Stays, Flights, etc.) for responsiveness. Check mobile viewport for small tap targets and layout consistency.
exit_criteria: Successfully navigate from index.html to tokyo.html via search. Confirm all top navigation links are clickable and responsive. Mobile viewport shows no critical layout errors.

phases.title: City/Area Hotel Lists
phases.objective: Test filtering, sorting, and navigation on tokyo.html (Tokyo list) and shinjuku.html (Shinjuku list).
key_checks: Interact with filters (price, stars, amenities) and sorting options. Click a hotel card to navigate to hotel-detail.html. Test 'Show on map' and other list features. Repeat critical interactions in mobile viewport.
exit_criteria: Successfully filter/sort results and navigate to a hotel detail page. Confirm map and list features are functional. Mobile viewport filters/sorting work as expected.

phases.title: Hotel Detail & Room Selection
phases.objective: Validate hotel detail page (hotel-detail.html) content, 'Reserve' flow, and room selection (room-selection.html).
key_checks: Review hotel details (location, amenities, reviews). Click 'Reserve' to proceed to room selection. Verify room details, price breakdown, and 'Continue to booking details' button. Check mobile viewport for responsive design.
exit_criteria: Successfully navigate from hotel-detail.html to room-selection.html. Confirm room details and price summary are accurate. Mobile viewport shows readable content and functional buttons.

phases.title: Booking & Confirmation
phases.objective: Test the reservation form (reservation.html) and confirmation page (confirmation.html) for usability, validation, and accessibility.
key_checks: Fill out reservation details (name, email, phone) and submit to reach confirmation.html. Verify confirmation page content (booking details, price, policies). Check form validation (e.g., required fields, email format). Test mobile viewport for form usability.
exit_criteria: Successfully submit reservation and reach confirmation.html. Confirm booking details are accurate. Mobile form interactions are smooth with proper validation.

phases.title: Adjacent Business Flows
phases.objective: Sample adjacent flows (Flights, Car Rentals, Attractions) to assess consistency and usability.
key_checks: Interact with search forms on each page (e.g., flight search, car rental search). Test primary actions (e.g., 'Search' for flights, 'View deal' for car rentals). Check responsive layout and mobile usability.
exit_criteria: Successfully complete a search action on each adjacent page. Confirm layout and functionality are consistent with the primary booking flow. Mobile viewport interactions are error-free.

phases.title: Recovery & Support Paths
phases.objective: Test recovery paths (e.g., 'Cancel booking', 'Manage your trips') and support pages (help.html, my-trips.html).
key_checks: From confirmation.html, test 'Cancel booking' and 'Manage your booking' links. Navigate to my-trips.html to view bookings. Test help.html search and FAQ navigation. Check mobile responsiveness for support actions.
exit_criteria: Successfully navigate recovery paths (e.g., cancel a booking, manage trips). Confirm help page functionality (search, FAQ access). Mobile viewport support actions are usable.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages (index, tokyo, shinjuku, hotel-detail, room-selection, reservation, confirmation, flights, car-rentals, attractions, help, my-trips).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls (search, filters, forms, navigation links) per key page. Test primary actions (search, reserve, book, confirm) and recovery actions (cancel, manage).
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks (search, form interactions, navigation) on mobile viewport for all key pages (index, tokyo, hotel-detail, reservation, confirmation).

notes: Max steps (80) should be sufficient to cover all phases, but prioritize the primary booking flow if time is limited. Document any console/network errors or layout warnings encountered during interactions.

findings.user_goal: Cancel an upcoming booking via my-trips.html
findings.problem: The 'Cancel booking' button on my-trips.html (mobile and desktop) does not trigger any visible cancellation process (e.g., confirmation dialog, navigation, or feedback) when clicked.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Cancel booking' button (ux-12) on my-trips.html resulted in no URL change, no dialog, and no visible page update. This was observed in both mobile and desktop viewports during testing.
findings.why_it_matters: Users relying on the cancellation feature to modify or cancel their bookings will be unable to do so, leading to frustration and potential loss of trust in the platform's recovery options.
findings.suggestion: Implement a confirmation dialog or clear feedback (e.g., 'Cancellation request submitted') when the 'Cancel booking' button is clicked. Ensure the cancellation flow includes validation and error handling to guide users through the process.

findings.user_goal: Navigate and interact with the booking system on mobile devices
findings.problem: Mobile viewports have small tap targets (e.g., 'Booking.com' 140x36px, 'JPY' 60x34px) below mobile usability guidelines (44x44px minimum), and horizontal overflow (page width > viewport width) causing layout issues.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings in mobile viewports show tap targets like 'Booking.com' (140x36px) and 'JPY' (60x34px) below 44x44px. Horizontal overflow (e.g., page width 633px > viewport 390px) was observed on confirmation.html and my-trips.html.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets increase the risk of misclicks, reducing usability for mobile users. Horizontal overflow forces users to scroll horizontally, creating a disjointed experience and potentially hiding content.
findings.suggestion: Adjust tap target sizes to meet mobile usability guidelines (e.g., 44x44px minimum) and ensure responsive design to eliminate horizontal overflow. Test mobile layouts across multiple devices to confirm consistency.

findings.user_goal: Complete the sign-in process to access account features
findings.problem: Clicking 'Continue with email' on signin.html navigates to index.html (home page) instead of progressing to the next sign-in step (e.g., password entry), breaking the sign-in flow.
findings.evidence: Testing the sign-in flow revealed that clicking 'Continue with email' after entering an email address redirected to index.html, failing to advance the sign-in process as expected.
findings.why_it_matters: A broken sign-in flow prevents users from accessing account-related features (e.g., saved bookings, preferences), reducing trust and usability for returning users.
findings.suggestion: Fix the 'Continue with email' button to navigate to the password entry or verification step (e.g., signin-password.html) instead of the home page. Ensure the sign-in flow is consistent and error-free.

findings.user_goal: Complete the booking form and submit it
findings.problem: The 'Complete booking' button remains disabled until all required fields (e.g., 'Your arrival time' dropdown) are visible and filled, but the form does not clearly indicate which fields are missing or required.
findings.evidence: During form testing, the 'Complete booking' button stayed disabled until scrolling revealed the 'Your arrival time' dropdown (a required field). No visible indicators (e.g., asterisks, error messages) marked required fields, leading to confusion about what was missing.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may struggle to identify required fields, delaying form completion and increasing frustration. Lack of feedback on required fields reduces transparency and usability.
findings.suggestion: Mark required fields with asterisks (*) and provide inline feedback (e.g., 'This field is required') for empty required fields. Ensure all required fields are visible or clearly indicated before submission.

findings.user_goal: Explore all business-line pages (e.g., flights, car rentals, attractions)
findings.problem: Many interactive elements on business-line pages (e.g., 'Airport taxis', 'Attractions' links on airport-taxis.html) remain untested, indicating incomplete feature coverage.
findings.evidence: The feature coverage percentage is only 5%, with many interactive elements (e.g., links on airport-taxis.html) untested. The 'open_questions' section lists untested controls like 'Airport taxis' and 'Attractions' links.
findings.why_it_matters: Incomplete feature coverage means potential usability issues in adjacent business flows (e.g., car rentals, attractions) may go unnoticed, impacting the overall user experience for users exploring multiple services.
findings.suggestion: Test all interactive elements across business-line pages (e.g., airport-taxis.html, car-rentals.html, attractions.html) to ensure consistency with the primary booking flow and identify any usability gaps.

findings.user_goal: Cancel a booking via the 'Cancel booking' button
findings.problem: The 'Cancel booking' button provides no feedback (e.g., loading state, confirmation dialog) when clicked, leaving users unsure if their cancellation request was received.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Cancel booking' button resulted in no visible change, no loading indicator, and no confirmation message, as observed in both mobile and desktop viewports.
findings.why_it_matters: Lack of feedback creates uncertainty, leading users to question if their action was successful or if the system is unresponsive. This reduces trust and increases user frustration.
findings.suggestion: Add a loading state (e.g., spinner) or confirmation dialog when the 'Cancel booking' button is clicked to indicate the system is processing the request. Provide clear feedback (e.g., 'Cancellation request submitted') upon completion.

gaps: Only directly exercised 5% of visible interactive feature signatures.
